objective: Verify that the frozen layer-3 expert-103 rank-four correction can be stored as a K3 down matrix plus BF16 factors, reconstructed when the expert is loaded, and executed with the same one-GEMM endpoint measured by the earlier dense screen.
evidence_boundary: This receipt proves bit-identical runtime closure and repeats the one-context KLD result. It does not provide document-level replication, a complete QSRT container, a complete-checkpoint byte ledger, or production-serving performance.

stored_factor_artifact.tensor_parallel_slice_closure: The stored base and factors reconstructed the stored FP16 candidate down slice bit for bit on tensor-parallel rank zero. The full model run exercised the same assertion on all four ranks.

dense_screen_closure.explanation_for_different_kld_file_hashe: The PyTorch container files carry different serialization metadata even though their loaded tensors are bit-identical.

two_gemm_control.decision: Do not execute the correction as two inference GEMMs. The additional intermediate rounding changed the expert output by about 2e-7 relative SSE on stored routed rows and erased most of the measured KLD gain after downstream propagation.

deployment_decision: Serialize the low-rank factors as checkpoint bookkeeping, fuse their product into the decoded FP16 down matrix when the expert is loaded, and execute the existing one-GEMM expert path. Independent document confirmation and exact complete-container accounting remain required before release.
